places.name: National Theatre of Costa Rica
places.ai_summary: The National Theatre of Costa Rica is a historic and architectural gem, showcasing stunning neoclassical design. It hosts cultural performances and offers guided tours.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on major holidays.

places.place_tip: Attend a live performance to experience the theatre's acoustics.

places.name: Pre-Columbian Gold Museum
places.ai_summary: The Pre-Columbian Gold Museum houses an extensive collection of gold artifacts from Costa Rica's indigenous cultures. It's an educational and cultural treasure trove.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on Mondays.

places.place_tip: Don't miss the detailed explanations of the goldsmithing techniques.
places.address: Plaza de la Cultura, San José, Costa Rica

places.name: Mercado Central (Central Market)
places.ai_summary: Mercado Central is a bustling market offering a variety of local goods, from fresh produce to traditional crafts. It's a great place to experience Costa Rican culture and cuisine.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited in the morning for fresh produce.

places.place_tip: Try the local dishes at one of the market's sodas (small eateries).
places.address: Avenida Central, San José, Costa Rica

places.name: National Museum of Costa Rica
places.ai_summary: The National Museum of Costa Rica offers a comprehensive overview of the country's history, from pre-Columbian times to the present. The museum is set in a beautiful building and has extensive gardens.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on Mondays.

places.place_tip: Explore the gardens for a peaceful retreat in the city.

places.name: Jade Museum
places.ai_summary: The Jade Museum in San José is home to the world's largest collection of pre-Columbian jade artifacts. The museum offers insights into the ancient cultures of Costa Rica.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on Sundays.

places.place_tip: Join a guided tour to fully appreciate the exhibits.

places.name: Barrio Amón Historic District
places.ai_summary: Barrio Amón is a charming historic district known for its well-preserved architecture and vibrant arts scene. It's a great area to explore on foot.

opening_hours.notes: Best explored on foot; some areas may be closed to traffic.

places.place_tip: Visit the local galleries and cafes tucked away in this artistic neighborhood.
places.address: Barrio Amón, San José, Costa Rica

places.name: La Sabana Metropolitan Park
places.ai_summary: La Sabana Metropolitan Park is a large urban park in San José, offering green spaces, walking paths, and a lake. It's a popular spot for both locals and tourists to relax and enjoy nature.

opening_hours.notes: Gates close at 20:00, but visitors can stay until 22:00.

places.place_tip: Rent a bike to explore the park more easily.

places.name: Costa Rican Art Museum
places.ai_summary: The Costa Rican Art Museum is located in La Sabana Metropolitan Park and features a wide range of Costa Rican art, from pre-Columbian to contemporary works. The museum is known for its beautiful gardens and architecture.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on Mondays.

places.place_tip: Check out the museum shop for unique Costa Rican handicrafts.

places.name: Plaza de la Cultura
places.ai_summary: Plaza de la Cultura is a central square in San José, surrounded by important buildings like the National Theatre and the Pre-Columbian Gold Museum. It's a hub of cultural and social activity.

opening_hours.notes: Always open, but best visited during the day.

places.place_tip: Enjoy a coffee at one of the nearby cafes and people-watch.

places.name: Metropolitan Cathedral
places.ai_summary: The Metropolitan Cathedral, also known as the Cathedral of San José, is the main church of San José. It features impressive neoclassical architecture and beautiful stained glass windows.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on major holidays.

places.place_tip: Be quiet and respectful inside the cathedral, as it is a place of worship.

places.name: Museo de los Niños (Children’s Museum)
places.ai_summary: Museo de los Niños is a vibrant children's museum in San José, offering interactive exhibits and educational programs. It's a great place for families to explore and learn together.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on Mondays.

places.place_tip: Check the schedule for special workshops or activities for children.

places.name: Avenida Central Shopping Street
places.ai_summary: Avenida Central is a bustling pedestrian street in the heart of San José, lined with shops, cafes, and street vendors. It's a popular spot for both locals and tourists to shop and socialize.

opening_hours.notes: Some shops may close earlier on Sundays.

places.place_tip: Bargain politely at street vendor stalls for souvenirs.

places.name: Parque Nacional
places.ai_summary: Parque Nacional is a beautiful national park located just outside San José. It features lush rainforests, hiking trails, and diverse wildlife. It's a great escape into nature from the city.

opening_hours.notes: Gates close at 18:00, but visitors can stay until 19:00.

places.place_tip: Bring water and snacks, and wear comfortable shoes for hiking.

places.name: Teatro Melico Salazar
places.ai_summary: Teatro Melico Salazar is a prominent theater in San José, known for hosting a variety of performances, including concerts, dance, and theater. The venue itself is an architectural landmark.

opening_hours.notes: Box office hours may vary; check the schedule for performances.

places.place_tip: Book tickets in advance for popular shows.

places.name: Spirogyra Butterfly Garden
places.ai_summary: The Spirogyra Butterfly Garden is a serene oasis in San José, featuring a wide variety of butterflies in a lush, tropical setting. It's a peaceful place to explore and learn about butterfly conservation.

opening_hours.notes: Closed on Mondays.

places.place_tip: Visit the garden in the morning when the butterflies are most active.

places.name: Cerro de la Muerte Day Trip
places.ai_summary: Cerro de la Muerte, or 'Death's Mountain', is a popular day trip from San José, offering stunning views, hiking trails, and a chance to see unique wildlife. The area is cooler due to its altitude.
places.name_english: Cerro de la Muerte Day Trip

opening_hours.notes: Gates close at 18:00, but visitors can stay until 19:00.

places.place_tip: Dress warmly, as it can be cold and windy at the top.
places.address: Cerro de la Muerte, San José, Costa Rica

places.name: Escazú Artisan Market
places.ai_summary: The Escazú Artisan Market is a vibrant market located in the Escazú district, just outside San José. It offers a wide range of artisanal products, including crafts, jewelry, and local foods.

opening_hours.notes: Best visited on weekends when more vendors are present.

places.place_tip: Look for unique souvenirs and try the local delicacies.

places.name: Museo del Jade Marco Fidel Tristán
places.ai_summary: Museo del Jade Marco Fidel Tristán is a museum dedicated to pre-Columbian jade artifacts, showcasing the importance of jade in Costa Rican history and culture.
places.name_english: Museo del Jade Marco Fidel Tristán

opening_hours.notes: Closed on Sundays.

places.place_tip: Combine your visit with the nearby National Museum for a full day of culture.

places.name: Café Britt Coffee Tour (Heredia)
places.ai_summary: The Café Britt Coffee Tour offers an in-depth look at Costa Rican coffee production, from bean to cup. The tour includes a walk through the coffee plantation and a tasting session.

opening_hours.notes: Reservations recommended for tours.

places.place_tip: Bring back some coffee beans as a souvenir.

places.name: Day Trip to Poás Volcano
places.ai_summary: A day trip to Poás Volcano includes a visit to one of Costa Rica's most famous volcanoes, known for its large crater and active fumaroles. The area around the volcano is rich in biodiversity.

opening_hours.notes: Check for volcanic activity updates before visiting.

places.place_tip: Wear warm clothing, as it can be cold and windy at the volcano.
